subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In batik, which material is applied to the fabric to resist the dye?
questions.explain: Batik is a resist technique in which hot wax blocks areas of cloth so they stay undyed.

questions.q: Which tool is used to push ink through the mesh in screen printing?
questions.explain: A squeegee is drawn across the screen to force ink through the open areas of the mesh onto the fabric.

questions.q: Why do tied areas in tie-dye stay a different colour from the rest of the cloth?
options: They resist the dye and remain undyed
They absorb extra dye and darken
They melt under the heat of the dye bath
They bleach lighter in the wash
questions.explain: Tie-dye is a resist method: tightly bound areas block the dye, leaving pale patterns.

questions.q: Appliqué is the technique of:
options: Stitching fabric shapes onto a background fabric
Dyeing fabric using a wax resist
Weaving threads together on a loom
questions.explain: Appliqué builds up an image or pattern by sewing cut fabric pieces onto a base cloth.

questions.q: In weaving, what are the warp threads?
options: The lengthwise threads held taut on the loom
questions.explain: The warp runs lengthwise on the loom while the weft is woven across it horizontally.

questions.q: Which natural fibre is obtained from sheep?
questions.explain: Wool is an animal fibre sheared from sheep.

questions.q: Cotton and linen are natural fibres derived from:
questions.explain: Cotton comes from the cotton plant and linen from the flax plant, so both are plant (cellulose) fibres.

questions.q: Which of these is a synthetic (man-made) fibre?
questions.explain: Polyester is manufactured from petrochemicals, unlike the natural fibres wool, silk and cotton.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a mordant in the dyeing process?
options: To fix the dye to the fibre and improve colourfastness
To bleach the cloth before dyeing
To add a shiny sheen to the surface
questions.explain: A mordant bonds the dye to the fibre so the colour holds and resists washing out.

questions.q: How is felt traditionally made?
options: By matting wool fibres together using moisture, heat and friction
By weaving cotton threads on a loom
By printing ink through a mesh screen
questions.explain: Felting interlocks and mats wool fibres with moisture, warmth and agitation to form a dense non-woven fabric.

questions.q: William Morris was a leading figure of which movement?
questions.explain: Morris helped found the Arts and Crafts movement and produced block-printed textiles such as 'Strawberry Thief'.

questions.q: Yinka Shonibare is well known for using which type of fabric in his work?
questions.explain: Shonibare uses brightly patterned Dutch wax (Ankara) batik cotton to explore identity, colonialism and cultural authenticity.

questions.q: In textiles, Grayson Perry is particularly known for producing large:
questions.explain: Perry is celebrated for large narrative tapestries such as 'The Vanity of Small Differences'.

questions.q: Faith Ringgold is best known for creating:
options: Narrative 'story quilts' that combine painting and fabric
questions.explain: Ringgold's story quilts blend painted images, text and pieced fabric to tell narratives about African-American life.

questions.q: Which technique is a form of resist dyeing that originated in Japan?
questions.explain: Shibori is a Japanese resist-dyeing method that binds, folds or stitches cloth before dyeing, often with indigo.

questions.q: A student wants to repeat a pattern by hand using a carved surface dipped in ink and pressed onto cloth. Which technique should they use?
questions.explain: Block printing stamps a repeating design onto fabric using an inked carved block.

questions.q: A designer needs a lightweight, breathable natural fabric for a summer garment. Which material is most suitable?
questions.explain: Cotton is a breathable, absorbent natural fibre well suited to cool, comfortable summer clothing.

questions.q: A student inspired by Yinka Shonibare wants to explore cultural identity through their textiles. Which approach best reflects his practice?
options: Using vibrant African wax-print fabrics to question cultural identity
Weaving plain undyed wool into a rug
questions.explain: Shonibare's use of patterned wax-print cloth to interrogate identity and cultural belonging is central to his work.

questions.q: Embroidery is best described as:
options: Decorating fabric using needle and thread stitches
Forcing ink through a mesh screen
questions.explain: Embroidery is the surface decoration of fabric with hand or machine stitching in thread.

questions.q: A student wants a soft, raised design made by stitching two layers of fabric together with padding (wadding) between them. Which technique should they use?
questions.explain: Quilting stitches layers of fabric around a wadding filling to create a padded, raised surface.
